subject: def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects
existing_correction: The set closure(C_p^+) minus {0} contains N_p, a timelike vector, so calling it the future closed null cone is incorrect. Both carriers now call it the future causal set. The exact set formula and proof are preserved; no outside consumer repeats the null-only identification.
actual_current_corrected_passages:
**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

subject: gr-connections-and-free-fall
existing_correction: Consumer check found exp_p o psi_p^{-1} labeled as coordinates although it maps coordinate tuples to M. Corrected exponential coordinate chart to psi_p o exp_p^{-1}:U_p -> R4; supplier theorem uses this exact direction.
actual_current_corrected_passages:
**Geodesics and exponential coordinates.** The geodesic initial-value problem
has a unique maximal solution $\gamma_{p,v}$ for every $(p,v)\in TM$; its flow
domain is open with smooth evaluation map, the scaling relation
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$ holds, and the exponential map
$\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$ is smooth on a star-shaped open domain with
$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}$, so it is a local diffeomorphism at the
origin ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]). The exponential
coordinate chart $\psi_p\circ\exp_p^{-1}$ then gives $g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$,
$\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$ at the point. In the
exponential chart, a geodesic through $p$ is the straight radial line while its
initial vector remains in the chosen star-shaped domain; no claim is made for a
later return to the chart after that vector leaves the domain. The theorem
explicitly claims nothing at second order
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]).

**Scope of the local-inertial reading.** The final item separates the
mathematics of normal coordinates from its physical reading
([[rem-gr-normal-coordinates-and-local-inertial-frames-scope]]): the identities
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$, $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$ are
first order at a single event; they assert nothing about second derivatives,
curvature or a neighborhood isometric to Minkowski space, they give no global
inertial frame and no relation between the exponential charts at different
points, and they are not an empirical equivalence-principle statement. The
standard sources for the page are Carroll, *Lecture Notes on General
Relativity* (Chs. 1-4), Reall, *Part III General Relativity* (§§3.1-3.4, 6.4)
and Tong, *General Relativity* (§§1.1, 3.2-3.3); the harvest, locators and
dispositions are recorded in the batch coverage file.

subject: rem-gr-no-universal-global-energy

- **A global energy needs a symmetry and control of the flux.** The Killing
  charge $Q_\xi$ of [[def-gr-killing-energy-charge]] exists only for a model
  that admits an everywhere timelike future-directed Killing field $\xi$;
  the theorem is conditional on this field and supplies no existence result

  slice of unbounded spatial extent one further needs
  the limiting flux and the integrals to converge; the flux theorem

  smooth singular chains and supplies no such limit, and the framework's scope
  note [[rem-gr-einstein-matter-scope-and-conventions]] already excludes
  arbitrary rough or noncompact domains from its smooth branch.

- **Empirical status.** The note contains no experiment, no measured input and

subject: lem-gr-lipschitz-family-limit-subsequence
existing_correction: Choose finite covers simultaneously and use lexicographically least infinite tuple classes, then least increasing indices. This deterministic recursion uses only AC_omega.
actual_current_corrected_passages: 1.1 (Deterministic diagonal extraction after countable choice.) Enumerate $D=\{q_1,q_2,\dots\}$ [L1]. Compactness gives a finite cover of $B$ by balls of radius $1/n$ for each $n\ge1$; [L3] chooses one ordered finite list of centers for each $n$, from this family fixed in advance. Set $A_0=\mathbb N$. At stage $n$, classify the indices $m\in A_{n-1}$ by the tuple of least ball indices containing $\sigma_m(q_1),\dots,\sigma_m(q_n)$ in the chosen radius-$1/n$ cover. There are finitely many classes, so at least one is infinite; let $A_n$ be the infinite class with lexicographically least tuple. This defines nested infinite sets by deterministic recursion, without dependent choice. Put $m_0=0$ and let $m_n$ be the least member of $A_n$ greater than $m_{n-1}$. For fixed $i$ and $n\ge i$, every $m_j$ with $j\ge n$ lies in $A_n$, so the values $\sigma_{m_j}(q_i)$ lie in one ball of radius $1/n$ and have pairwise distances less than $2/n$. They are Cauchy and converge by [L2]. Write $\sigma(q_i)=\lim_j\sigma_{m_j}(q_i)$. The only choice was the simultaneous selection of finite covers. [L1, L2, L3, choose, construct]

3.1 (Uniform convergence on compact subintervals.) Let $[a,b]\subseteq I$ be a compact subinterval and let $\varepsilon>0$. Choose finitely many points $q_1,\dots,q_N\in D$ such that every $t\in[a,b]$ satisfies $|t-q_i|\le\varepsilon/(3K+3)$ for some $i$; this is possible, including when $a=b$, because $D$ is dense in $I$ and a compact interval is totally bounded in the sense of admitting such finite nets, the case $K=0$ being immediate from the estimator below with $\varepsilon/(3K+3)$ read as any positive number. Since $\sigma_{m_j}(q_i)\to\sigma(q_i)$ for each $i$, there is $j_0$ such that $d(\sigma_{m_j}(q_i),\sigma(q_i))<\varepsilon/3$ for all $j\ge j_0$ and all $i\le N$. For $t\in[a,b]$ pick $i$ with $|t-q_i|\le\varepsilon/(3K+3)$; then $$d(\sigma_{m_j}(t),\sigma(t))\le d(\sigma_{m_j}(t),\sigma_{m_j}(q_i))+d(\sigma_{m_j}(q_i),\sigma(q_i))+d(\sigma(q_i),\sigma(t))<\frac\varepsilon3+\frac\varepsilon3+\frac\varepsilon3=\varepsilon$$ for $j\ge j_0$, because both $\sigma_{m_j}$ and $\sigma$ are $K$-Lipschitz. subject: lem-gr-maximal-flow-escape
existing_correction: Use compact tail closures and a local countable chart basis to obtain a subsequence without global metrization.
actual_current_corrected_passages:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $M$ be a smooth
manifold without boundary, let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), let $p\in M$ and
let $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ be the unique maximal integral curve of $X$
with $\gamma(0)=p$ ([[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]],
[[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]]). If $\beta<+\infty$ then for every
compact set $K\subseteq M$
([[def-compact-space]]) there is $s\in(\alpha,\beta)$ such that
$\gamma(t)\notin K$ for every $t\in(s,\beta)$. Dually, if $\alpha>-\infty$
then for every compact $K$ there is $s$ such that $\gamma(t)\notin K$ for
every $t\in(\alpha,s)$.

[L3] Every sequence in a compact subset $K$ of a Hausdorff manifold has a convergent subsequence. Indeed, the closures in $K$ of its tails are nonempty closed sets with the finite-intersection property, so compactness gives a point $q$ in their intersection. A chart at $q$ supplies the countable neighborhood basis of coordinate balls of radii tending to zero; recursively taking the least index beyond the preceding index whose term lies in that ball gives a subsequence converging to $q$. This proves the needed sequential compactness without invoking a global metrization theorem ([[def-compact-space]], [[def-smooth-manifold]]).

actual_current_corrected_passages: [L4] Positivity: for a positive smooth density $\mu_r(O)>0$ for every nonempty open $O$, and $r>0$ on a nonempty open set means the coefficient in any chart meeting that set is positive on a nonempty open subset of the chart image ([[cor-positive-density-measures-assign-positive-volume-to-nonempty-open-sets-and-metric-balls]], [[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]]).

- **Why the weights $2^{-i}c_i$.** Without finite weights a positive smooth density can have infinite total mass; the weights make $\mu_{r_0}(M)\le1$ while keeping every term positive, and the $c_i$ control the individual total masses. The construction uses $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ only through the existence of the countable partition of unity and the finite selections inside compactly supported pieces.
- **The measure is not canonical.** Any two measures produced this way are mutually absolutely continuous with positive smooth density ratio, but the normalization depends on the chosen cover and partition. Only the properties (a)-(c) are used downstream, and they are stable under replacing $r$ by $\lambda r$, $\lambda>0$.
- **Use.** The measure $\mu$ is the finite volume underlying [[lem-gr-chronological-volume-continuity]] and the volume time function of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]]; clause (c) is what makes achronal boundaries and other local Lipschitz graphs null via [[lem-gr-achronal-boundaries-lipschitz-graphs]] clause (d).

subject: lem-gr-locally-finite-shell-sum
existing_correction: Use all admissible bump tuples to obtain finite covers per shell, select countably many finite tuple lists, retain repeated centers as separate indices, and define W by an open gradient locus.
actual_current_corrected_passages: 1.2 (A locally finite family of cone bumps.) For each connected component $M_\alpha$ of $M$ fix a base point $m_\alpha$ and write $B^\alpha_R:=\{q\in M_\alpha:d_{h'}(q,m_\alpha)<R\}$; the components are open and at most countable [L3], so $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ selects the base points. Since $S_b$ is closed and meets only countably many components, and each $S_b\cap M_\alpha$ is covered by the shells $A^\alpha_m:=S_b\cap(\overline{B^\alpha_m}\setminus B^\alpha_{m-1})$, $m\ge1$ (with $B^\alpha_0:=\emptyset$), which are closed in $M_\alpha$ and $d_{h'}$-bounded hence compact [L3], we obtain: $S_b=\bigcup_{\alpha,m}A^\alpha_m$ with each $A^\alpha_m$ compact. For each shell consider all admissible tuples $(x,C,h)$ supplied by [L2], with $x\in A^\alpha_m$ and $\operatorname{diam}_{h'}(C)<1$. Their sets $\{h>1/2\}$ cover the shell, because a tuple exists at every center. Compactness supplies a finite list of tuples covering each shell; Countable Choice selects one such finite list for each of the countably many shells. Index every selected tuple separately, retaining repetitions of a center, by a countable index set $F$, and write its data as $(x_j,C_j,h_j)$ for $j\in F$. The family $\{C_j\}_{j\in F}$ is locally finite: if a tuple from shell $A^\alpha_m$ has $C_j\cap B^\alpha_R\ne\varnothing$, then $x_j\in C_j$ and its diameter is less than one, so $d_{h'}(x_j,m_\alpha)<R+1$. Since the center is in that shell, $m<R+2$. Only finitely many shells satisfy this bound in a fixed component, and each supplied finitely many tuples. Components are open, so this proves local finiteness everywhere. Define $h^+:=\sum_{j\in F}h_j$, smooth by [L4]. It is nonnegative, zero on $\{t\le a\}$, and greater than $1/2$ on $S_b$. At a point $q\in\{h^+>0\}\cap\{t\le b\}$ only finitely many terms contribute. Each gradient is past timelike or zero by [L2], and some term is positive and therefore has a past timelike gradient. Their sum is past timelike by [L5]. [L2, L3, L4, L5, given, choose]

- **What the local finiteness buys.** The sum $\sum_{x\in F}h_x$ is over a countable family, but the diameter-one property of the supports makes it a locally finite family, so the sum is smooth without any convergence assumptions; this is the only place where the auxiliary metric of [L3] is used, and it uses the properness of its distance, not the volume time.
- **Time reversal.** The negative plateau $h^-$ is manufactured from the time-reversed cone bumps; its gradient is past timelike exactly where $\varphi'<0$ and the reversed bumps are future timelike, which is the set where the weak step is genuinely changing.
- **Use.** The weak steps $\tau$ of this lemma, taken for finitely many levels, are averaged in [[lem-gr-strip-weak-steps]] to cover a whole inner strip with a strictly timelike gradient, and the resulting strip functions are summed in [[thm-gr-smooth-cauchy-temporal-splitting]] to produce a global smooth time function.

subject: lem-gr-strip-weak-steps
existing_correction: Cover each compact K_j with all admissible tuples and choose countably many finite tuple lists; average the individually indexed steps.
actual_current_corrected_passages: 1.1 (Finite lists of weak steps for each compact slice.) For $j\ge1$ put $K_j:=L_j\cap\{a'\le t\le c'\}$, compact by [L3]. Consider all tuples $(b,\tau,U)$ with $b\in[a',c']$, $\tau$ a weak step supplied by [L1] with outer bounds $a,c$, and $U$ its open past-timelike-gradient locus containing $S_b$. Their open sets cover $K_j$, since at $x\in K_j$ a tuple exists with $b=t(x)$. Compactness supplies a finite tuple list covering $K_j$. For empty $K_j$, a single tuple at $b=(a'+c')/2$ is available, so every list may be taken nonempty. Countable Choice selects one nonempty finite list for each $j$. Write its entries $(b_{j,i},\tau_{j,i},U_{j,i})$, $1\le i\le m_j$. No weak-step family indexed by all real levels is selected. [L1, L3, given, choose]

- **Why the average is needed.** A single weak step has a timelike gradient only near its own level, so a compact slice is covered by finitely many such neighborhoods and the average turns this cover into one function that is strictly timelike on the whole slice; the exhaustion then lets countably many slice functions be summed with rapidly decaying coefficients.
- **Why the gradient bounds are enough.** The coefficients $2^{-j}A_j^{-1}$ only have to absorb the bounds on the first $j$ boxes through order $j$, so each derivative series is dominated there by $\sum_j2^{-j}$; no uniformity in the point is needed beyond compactness of the boxes.
- **Use.** The strip functions are the building blocks of [[thm-gr-smooth-cauchy-temporal-splitting]]: applied to the strips $[j-2,j+2]$ with inner strip $[j-1,j+1]$, their paired sum is a global temporal function.

subject: thm-gr-smooth-cauchy-temporal-splitting
existing_correction: Use (T(p),Phi(-T(p),p)); make the local-finiteness time buffer strict.
actual_current_corrected_passages: [L7] Flow theory: maximal integral curves of a smooth vector field exist uniquely; a vector field is complete exactly when all its maximal integral curves are defined on $\mathbb R$, equivalently exactly when its flow is global, and a global flow is a smooth map $\Phi:\mathbb R\times M\to M$ with $\Phi(0,p)=p$, $\Phi(s,\Phi(r,p))=\Phi(s+r,p)$ and $s\mapsto\Phi(s,p)$ an integral curve ([[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]], [[def-complete-vector-field]], [[prop-a-vector-field-is-complete-if-and-only-if-its-flow-is-global]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]).

5.1 (Levels are Cauchy hypersurfaces.) By [L4] and step 2.1, $T$ is a time function: $T(\gamma(a))<T(\gamma(b))$ for every future causal curve not constant on $[a,b]$. Let $c\in\mathbb R$. Every inextendible causal curve meets $S_c:=T^{-1}(c)$ in at least one parameter value: for a future-directed curve, $s\mapsto T(\gamma(s))$ is continuous with limits $-\infty$ at the past end (dual of step 4.1) and $+\infty$ at the future end (step 4.1), so [L8] gives a parameter with value $c$; the past-directed case is dual. It meets $S_c$ at most once, because two distinct parameter values would give two causally related distinct points with equal $T$-value, contradicting strict monotonicity. Hence $S_c$ is a Cauchy set; in particular $T$ is surjective. Since $dT
e0$ everywhere (the gradient is timelike), $S_c$ is an embedded hypersurface by [L6], and its tangent space at $p$ is $\ker dT_p=(
abla T_p)^\perp$, which is positive definite because $
abla T_p$ is timelike [L6]. Hence $S_c$ is a spacelike embedded hypersurface and a Cauchy set, that is, a Cauchy hypersurface; this is (b). [step 2.1, step 4.1, L4, L6, L8]

subject: lem-gr-strip-weak-steps
existing_correction: Use retrieved Bernal-Sanchez primary papers with exact relevant lemma/proposition locators; distinguish local formulas from source context.
actual_current_corrected_passages: ## Remarks

- **Why the average is needed.** A single weak step has a timelike gradient only near its own level, so a compact slice is covered by finitely many such neighborhoods and the average turns this cover into one function that is strictly timelike on the whole slice; the exhaustion then lets countably many slice functions be summed with rapidly decaying coefficients.
- **Why the gradient bounds are enough.** The coefficients $2^{-j}A_j^{-1}$ only have to absorb the bounds on the first $j$ boxes through order $j$, so each derivative series is dominated there by $\sum_j2^{-j}$; no uniformity in the point is needed beyond compactness of the boxes.
- **Use.** The strip functions are the building blocks of [[thm-gr-smooth-cauchy-temporal-splitting]]: applied to the strips $[j-2,j+2]$ with inner strip $[j-1,j+1]$, their paired sum is a global temporal function.

By the chain rule, $\frac{d}{ds}T(\gamma(s))=dT(X)(\gamma(s))=1$, so $T(\gamma(s))=T(z)+s$ throughout its domain. Suppose $\beta<+\infty$ and choose $s_0\in(\alpha,\beta)$. Define the smooth increasing bijection $\theta:[0,\infty)\to[s_0,\beta)$ by $\theta(u)=\beta-(\beta-s_0)e^{-u}$ and set $\widehat\gamma(u)=\gamma(\theta(u))$. This is a future causal curve. The escape lemma [L8] says the maximal flow line leaves every compact set as $s\to\beta$, so $\gamma(s)$ has no limit there; therefore $\widehat\gamma$ has no future endpoint limit and is future-inextendible. Apply the one-sided extension [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]] clause (d) to obtain an inextendible future causal curve $\widehat\gamma^*$ which agrees with $\widehat\gamma$ on $[0,\infty)$. By step 4.1, $T(\widehat\gamma^*(u))\to+\infty$ as $u\to\infty$. But on this same tail $T(\widehat\gamma(u))=T(z)+\theta(u)\to T(z)+\beta<+\infty$, a contradiction. Hence $\beta=+\infty$; the time-reversed argument gives $\alpha=-\infty$. Therefore every maximal integral curve is defined on $\mathbb R$, so $X$ is complete by [L7]; its flow is global and smooth. [step 3.2, step 4.1, L3, L7, L8]

- **Scope of the choice assumptions.** The construction uses $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ to select the countably many strip functions and their data, and $\mathrm{DC}$ enters through the escape lemma's compactness-to-sequences step and the limit curve conventions; no stronger form of choice is used.
- **Two time functions.** The continuous volume time $t$ of [[thm-gr-volume-time-function]] is the scaffold on which the smooth $T$ is built; $t$ itself is not smooth in general, and no smoothness of $t$ is claimed or used.
- **Use.** The splitting supplies the smooth Cauchy foliation and the complete orthogonal flow used by the GR14 symmetric-hyperbolic reduction and by the maximal globally hyperbolic development arguments of GR15.

Fix $(t_0,z_0)$ and put $\gamma(s):=x^{-1}(\sigma(s+T(t_0)),z_0)$. Since $\sigma$ takes values in $(0,1)$, the curve stays in $M$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$; it is smooth; and by the chain rule and [L2] its $t$-coordinate satisfies $\frac{d}{ds}\sigma(s+T(t_0))=\sigma'(s+T(t_0))=\frac1{T'(\sigma(s+T(t_0)))}$. Hence the chart velocity of $\gamma$ is $\bigl(1/T'(t),0,0,0\bigr)=X(\gamma(s))$ in the chart components, so $\gamma$ is an integral curve of $X$ defined on all of $\mathbb R$. The maximal integral curve of $X$ through any point therefore has domain $\mathbb R$ (an integral curve defined on a larger interval cannot exist because $\gamma$ covers the whole maximal interval: the uniqueness theorem identifies all integral curves through a common point on overlaps), so $X$ is complete and its flow $\Phi:\mathbb R\times M\to M$ is global and smooth ([[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]], [[def-complete-vector-field]], [[prop-a-vector-field-is-complete-if-and-only-if-its-flow-is-global]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]). subject: lem-gr-finite-smooth-volume-density
existing_correction: Derive the absolute-Jacobian density transformation from the determinant identity in arbitrary charts; clarify the constant-box comparison used for finite Borel integrals.
actual_current_corrected_passages: [L2] Densities as coefficients: a nonnegative density on $M$ assigns to every chart a Borel coefficient taking values in $[0,\infty]$ and obeying the absolute-Jacobian overlap law; products of coefficients with nonnegative smooth functions and locally finite sums obey the same law, so the product of a nonnegative smooth function with a density and every locally finite sum of densities are again densities; a density is smooth when all its chart coefficients are smooth ([[def-borel-measurable-nonnegative-density-on-a-manifold]]). In arbitrary overlapping charts with transition $x=\varphi\circ y$, tensor transformation gives $g_y=(D\varphi)^T(g_x\circ\varphi)D\varphi$, hence $\sqrt{|\det g_y|}=|\det D\varphi|\sqrt{|\det(g_x\circ\varphi)|}$. Thus the coefficients $w=\sqrt{|\det g_{ab}|}$ obey the density overlap law and define a positive smooth density without requiring an orientation. This is a determinant identity; the oriented volume-form assertion is not used ([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (a) for the coefficient formula).

4.1 (The properties of $\mu$.) By step 3.1, $\mu(M)=1$; since $r$ is a positive smooth density, [L3] makes $\mu$ compact-finite, locally finite, $\sigma$-finite and regular Borel. This is (a). Property (b) is the positivity clause of [L4]. For (c), let $(V,y)$ be a chart and let $E\subseteq V$ be Borel with $y(E)$ Lebesgue null. By the chart formula of [L5] applied with a partition whose first chart is $(V,y)$ and using $0\cdot\infty=0$, $\mu(E)$ is the sum of Lebesgue integrals of nonnegative Borel coefficients over $y(E)$ and over the images of the remaining charts, and each of those images is null in its own chart because the chart transitions are $C^1$ diffeomorphisms on overlaps and carry null sets to null sets [L6]; each integral vanishes by [L6], so $\mu(E)=0$. subject: lem-gr-lipschitz-family-limit-subsequence
existing_correction: Choose rational net points in I rather than inside the compact subinterval, preserving convergence even on an irrational singleton.
actual_current_corrected_passages:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(B,d)$ be a compact metric space
([[def-metric-space]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior, let $K\ge0$ be real, and let $\sigma_m:I\to B$,
$m\in\mathbb N$, be $K$-Lipschitz maps,
$d(\sigma_m(s),\sigma_m(t))\le K|s-t|$ for all $s,t\in I$. Then there are a
strictly increasing sequence $m_1<m_2<\cdots$ and a $K$-Lipschitz map
$\sigma:I\to B$ such that $\sigma_{m_j}\to\sigma$ uniformly on every compact
subinterval of $I$.

3.1 (Uniform convergence on compact subintervals.) Let $[a,b]\subseteq I$ be a compact subinterval and let $\varepsilon>0$. Choose finitely many points $q_1,\dots,q_N\in D$ such that every $t\in[a,b]$ satisfies $|t-q_i|\le\varepsilon/(3K+3)$ for some $i$; this is possible, including when $a=b$, because $D$ is dense in $I$ and a compact interval is totally bounded in the sense of admitting such finite nets, the case $K=0$ being immediate from the estimator below with $\varepsilon/(3K+3)$ read as any positive number. Since $\sigma_{m_j}(q_i)\to\sigma(q_i)$ for each $i$, there is $j_0$ such that $d(\sigma_{m_j}(q_i),\sigma(q_i))<\varepsilon/3$ for all $j\ge j_0$ and all $i\le N$. For $t\in[a,b]$ pick $i$ with $|t-q_i|\le\varepsilon/(3K+3)$; then $$d(\sigma_{m_j}(t),\sigma(t))\le d(\sigma_{m_j}(t),\sigma_{m_j}(q_i))+d(\sigma_{m_j}(q_i),\sigma(q_i))+d(\sigma(q_i),\sigma(t))<\frac\varepsilon3+\frac\varepsilon3+\frac\varepsilon3=\varepsilon$$ for $j\ge j_0$, because both $\sigma_{m_j}$ and $\sigma$ are $K$-Lipschitz. Hence $\sigma_{m_j}\to\sigma$ uniformly on $[a,b]$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, L2, given, discharge-construct] ∎

- **Why the flat case is transparent.** In an inertial chart the exponential map is a translation and the squared displacement is a quadratic form, so $Q$ is an ordinary quadratic function and the only analytic input is the flatness of $\varphi$ at $0$; in a curved manifold the same computation is performed after the exponential map linearises the cone.
